html:
The Tseshaht are a Nuu-chah-nulth First Nation of central Vancouver Island, British Columbia, living around Alberni Inlet and the Alberni Valley. The nation joined together many local groups along the inlet. Their name comes from Tsishaa, an ancestral village in Barkley Sound.

Like other Nuu-chah-nulth peoples they lived from the sea and rivers, on salmon, herring, shellfish and sea mammals, and built cedar plank houses and dugout canoes. Their main reserve today is at Port Alberni, where they live beside the Hupacasath of the upper valley. The Alberni Indian Residential School, which ran in their territory until 1973, is remembered for the abuse of the children sent there, part of Canada's residential school system.
